images.caption: Figure 2:Redundancy of dense full self-attention.Most target regions have been observed in historical frames and require only sparse geometric correspondences for faithful reconstruction, while newly revealed regions benefit from broader contextual interactions.

Figure 3:System Overview.For each target chunk, SPARC establishes token-level correspondences with historical observations through local geometric projection, and then prunes the backbone’s native self-attention to focus on geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context for previously observed regions, while newly revealed regions retain dense attention for flexible content synthesis. Historical RoPE re-indexing is employed to eliminate artificial temporal ordering biases among retrieved historical observations.
The generated observations are subsequently appended to the history bank for continuous rollout.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on DL3DV-Eval.Given the same input image and camera trajectory, we show frames generated with different methods along the roaming time.
Explicit-3D baselines drift from the target trajectory or accumulate geometric distortions, and implicit baselines fail to follow the prescribed camera path, whereas SPARC preserves scene appearance and accurate camera control throughout the rollout.See Supp. for additional scenes and video comparisons.

Figure 6:Qualitative comparison of revisitation on WorldScore-Static.Each scene follows a closed-loop camera trajectory (top view), and frames are sampled along the roaming time.
Baselines either distort the scene or fail to recover the originally observed content upon revisiting, whereas our SPARC faithfully restores the scene at both revisits.See Supp. for additional scenes and video comparisons.

Figure 7:Ablation on attention pruning and historical RoPE indexing.Progressively incorporating geometric correspondence, local window attention, and correspondence bias improves camera adherence and reconstruction fidelity.
The bottom rows visualize the pixel-wise difference|Δ||\Delta|between outputs generated using the original and shuffled history orders:
sequential history RoPE yields discrepancies that grow along the trajectory, whereas our shared indexing remains invariant.
Figure 8:Attention weight visualization.Given target queries, dense attention with the camera adapter exhibits attention peaks that deviate from geometrically corresponding historical regions.

Figure 9:Additional long-horizon generation results.Without any degradation-aware augmentation, SPARC generates high-fidelity, minute-long videos with precise camera adherence and persistent scene consistency.

Figure 10:Training-free dynamic scene generation.We segment the foreground object and shift its correspondence locations along a prescribed motion trajectory, allowing SPARC to synthesize natural object motion consistent with the specified trajectory.
